title: Add provenance-aware succinctness gate and sample prioritizer CI hook
author: Priya Nair
release_notes: Introduce a provenance-weighted succinctness gate and sample prioritizer to reduce spurious regression noise from verbosity changes; CI hook will surface high-impact brevity regressions and prioritize samples for human review.
description:
Motivation: We frequently see CI noise from changes that affect response length (verbosity) rather than core correctness. This PR adds a provenance-aware succinctness gate that uses prompt provenance and historical succinctness baselines to determine whether a length/verbosity regression is material, and a sample prioritizer that surfaces examples where succinctness shifts likely affect downstream quality.

Design summary: single continuous CI hook implemented as a lightweight orchestration step that runs after existing regression metrics. It computes a succinctness delta per prompt cohort, weights deltas by provenance (source, user segment, and anchor stability), and applies a threshold policy that can be tuned per-team. Samples that exceed the importance threshold are prioritized into a human-review queue and attached to the eval report.

Checklist:
- [x] Add succinctness metric and provenance weighting model (compact stats-based estimator)
- [x] Implement CI hook integration and config knobs (per-cohort thresholds, severity levels)
- [x] Add prioritizer that exports review artefacts and annotated traces
- [x] Unit tests for metric calculations and thresholds
- [x] Lightweight e2e smoke test that runs in CI (sample fixtures)
- [x] Docs: README + migration notes for teams to opt-in

Commits summary: see commits field for granular messages. High-level: initial metric + estimator, hook integration, prioritizer + exporter, tests and docs, CI flake fixes.

Changed areas / intent: This is intentionally non-breaking and off by default (teams opt-in by adding the hook to their eval config). It focuses on reducing false-positive regression signals coming from harmless verbosity changes while ensuring genuinely impactful brevity shifts are surfaced.

Review & testing notes: The hook was exercised in a canary pipeline against production prompt cohorts for two weeks. We tuned the default threshold to keep actioned samples below 0.5% of overall eval runs while capturing >90% of historical brevity-related incidents in our labelled corpus. CI runs initially saw a flaky smoke test (timing-related) which was hardened.

Merge: Squash-merged to main after sign-off.
